A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete main text and Appendices A-C. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v5 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, unseen-paper abstract generation results, and attention-head analyses in Sections 5-6 and Appendices B-C.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark scores, ablations, and the analyses in Appendices B-C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the reward-feedback procedure, experience buffer, and ICRL Preset and Autonomous strategies are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Game of 24, creative writing, ScienceWorld, AIME, HMMT, and unseen-paper abstract generation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The experiment-specific comparator sets are unchanged, including CoT-only, Long-CoT, Best-of-N, Self-Refine, and Reflexion in Game of 24, and ReAct in the ScienceWorld comparison.

E3.justification: Sections 5-6 and Appendices B-C retain the same models, sample sizes, context lengths, trial budgets, reward functions, evaluation metrics, and response-selection procedures.

E4.justification: Both retain the reward, context, and instruction ablations; context-length and compute analyses; unseen-abstract experiment; and reward-sensitive attention-head analysis. Their questions and supporting evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Standard-error reporting, the disclosed additional creative-writing runs, and Appendix C.2's Pearson-correlation tests and significance threshold are unchanged. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting information is added.

E6.justification: All reported table values and plotted results match. For example, Table 1 retains 90% for ICRL Preset and 49% for Best-of-N; Appendix C.1 retains 0.59 ROUGE-recall for ICRL. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Section 2's MDP, policy, context, and token-generation definitions and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. Neither version adds a theorem, proof, or revised formal assumption relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about emergent inference-time RL, scalar-reward prompting, and improvements over self-revision methods. The added code-release statement does not alter these scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of exploration and exploitation, learning versus search, and reward-sensitive attention remain unchanged. The qualification that self-evaluation may have a lower performance ceiling than external feedback is also retained.

D1.justification: v6 adds 'We release all code at:' and the garified/ICRL-for-LLM-Agent repository address to the abstract; v5 lacks this implementation-access pointer. Other technical disclosures are unchanged. The PDFs alone do not verify the repository's availability or contents.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to prior ICRL, self-revision, search, and prompt-optimization research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a short code-release statement, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Existing prose, terminology, and section order otherwise remain unchanged; apparent passage moves result from pagination.

P2.justification: The expanded abstract causes limited reflow across pages 1-9, including moving the Section 3 heading to page 4 and shifting figures and tables vertically. Display contents and captions remain unchanged; pages 10-24 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v6 modestly improves reproducibility documentation by providing a concrete implementation-access pointer absent from v5. The scientific content and appendices remain unchanged, and layout differences are limited. This benefit concerns documented access; the supplied PDFs do not establish the repository's completeness or usability.
